segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Welcome to Psalm Nights. [pause 3]

Get comfortable. There is nowhere else you need to be. [pause 5]

Tonight is Psalm 91. It is a psalm many people pray at night, and over their families. It is full of pictures of shelter. A secret place. A shadow. Wings. A shield. [pause 5]

We will read it twice, slowly. [pause 8]

verses.text: He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.
I will say of the LORD, He is my refuge and my fortress: my God; in him will I trust.
Surely he shall deliver thee from the snare of the fowler, and from the noisome pestilence.
He shall cover thee with his feathers, and under his wings shalt thou trust: his truth shall be thy shield and buckler.
Thou shalt not be afraid for the terror by night; nor for the arrow that flieth by day;
Nor for the pestilence that walketh in darkness; nor for the destruction that wasteth at noonday.
A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand; but it shall not come nigh thee.
Only with thine eyes shalt thou behold and see the reward of the wicked.
Because thou hast made the LORD, which is my refuge, even the most High, thy habitation;
There shall no evil befall thee, neither shall any plague come nigh thy dwelling.
For he shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways.
They shall bear thee up in their hands, lest thou dash thy foot against a stone.
Thou shalt tread upon the lion and adder: the young lion and the dragon shalt thou trample under feet.
Because he hath set his love upon me, therefore will I deliver him: I will set him on high, because he hath known my name.
He shall call upon me, and I will answer him: I will be with him in trouble; I will deliver him, and honour him.
With long life will I satisfy him, and shew him my salvation.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
He that dwelleth in the secret place. The psalm starts with where you live, not with what you fear. [pause 6]

The picture in verse four is a bird gathering her young under her wings. Feathers over them, warm and close, while the night goes on outside. [pause 6]

This psalm has been prayed in hospitals and in war, in storms and in long nights waiting for a phone call. It does not say that nothing hard will ever happen. It says, I will be with him in trouble. [pause 10]

One companion verse tonight. [pause 4]

verses.text: I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, LORD, only makest me dwell in safety.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
In peace. Lying down. Sleeping. Dwelling in safety, because of the Lord alone. [pause 6]

Here is Psalm 91 once more. You might picture those wings as you listen. [pause 10]

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Now let the words go quiet. [pause 8]

You do not have to hold on to them. They will be there in the morning. [pause 10]

Let your shoulders drop. Let your hands open. Let the bed hold the weight of you. [pause 12]

If a worry comes back, you can hand it over again. As many times as it takes. [pause 12]

The night is long and quiet, and you are not alone in it. [pause 15]

Feel the quiet of the room. The small sounds. The dark. Nothing is asked of you here. [pause 20]

You are held, the psalm said. You are known. You are kept. [pause 20]

Rest now. [pause 45]

first_reader.note: Written by Claude in the landing session, then Claude's pastor and cultural read.

pastor.note: Every psalm and companion is stored KJV pasted by code; reflections paraphrase in short echoes (no 8+ word typed scripture) and stay with each psalm's own point (shepherd, evening rest, keeping, shelter, stillness, quiet soul, being known, waiting, a shield in flight, light and waiting). No promise of sleep or protection: Psalm 91 says plainly it does not promise nothing hard will happen; Proverbs 3:24 framed as 'not a promise for every night'. God never quoted in first person outside scripture. Headings (Ps 3, Absalom) used only as the text's own titles.

cultural.note: Plain, unhurried English a tired woman at 11 PM can follow; no filler, no church jargon unexplained; hospital and grief named gently; shared rests vary their wording so the close is not the same sentence every night; pacing tuned only by silence (pauses) to 13.6-15.3 minutes.
